$Comment: What a player sees each time one step of a quest they are carrying moves: an ordinary tick
shows the step and how far along it is, and the tick that finishes the step says so instead.
This is the library's own neutral default. A mod that ships a file with this same name in its
own pack replaces it, and a server owner can do the same from the owner layer.
The moment carries 'quest' (its id), 'title' (its name in the reader's language), 'objective'
(the step's id), 'step' (the step's own sentence in the reader's language, for instance
'Break 12 logs'), 'current' and 'required' (how far along, out of how many), 'finished'
(true on the tick that completes the step) and 'source' (the one step this notice is about).
'player' is always the name of who moved it.
A step that moves quickly keeps to ONE line: each tick rewrites the notice already on screen
instead of adding another under it, so a player milling twenty logs still sees their pickups
and their finds rather than a column of counters. The line is kept per 'source', so three
steps moving at once keep three lines. Add "Merge": false to a Toast to have every tick
queue up instead, at the cost of the rest of the feed.
EveryPercent keeps a long step from chattering even so: an ordinary tick shows only when it
crosses a multiple of that many percent of the way (25 gives the quarter marks); the finishing
tick always shows. Delete it to show every tick. A mod that lets each player pick how chatty
their own screen is decides for them and is told whether the tick crossed a mark.
The Variants entry swaps the whole Toast for the finishing tick, so its wording and tone can
differ from an ordinary tick's without a second file: an ordinary tick is neutral Info, the
finish is green Success. A variant replaces the whole group rather than editing it, so every
leaf it does not restate is back to its own default - which is why the finish still lands ON
the counter it finishes rather than beside it. Tone colours the in-page frame and the words,
and picks the matching corner-feed style.
